_comment: ILLUSTRATIVE SCHEMA EXAMPLE. meta.research_access is full | search_only | none; meeting and meeting_date may be left empty. 'Vireo Inspection' is fictional; do not reuse any fact below. Inline markup: **bold**, *italic*, [n] or [1,3] cites source n, {CR} company-reported, {INF} analyst inference, {UNK} unknown. Sections take a string (one paragraph), a list (bullets), or {"text": ..., "bullets": [...]}.

meta.meeting: Intro call with CEO and CTO
meta.research_basis: Independent web research plus supplied deck

company.name: Vireo Inspection
company.one_liner: Inline weld-seam inspection for automotive body shops that learns new part variants from a few dozen labeled images, attacking the retraining cost that stalls most vision QA rollouts.

sections.company_product: Vireo sells a camera-plus-software station that inspects resistance spot and laser welds on body-in-white lines and flags defects before paint. Buyers are plant quality and manufacturing engineering leads at OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers. The value case is catching weld defects that today rely on destructive teardown sampling.

technology.text: Structured-light 3D capture feeds a defect model pre-trained on a large weld image corpus, then adapted per line with few-shot fine-tuning {CR}.
bullets: **Claimed edge:** new variant onboarding in days rather than the weeks typical for rules-based machine vision [3] {CR}.
**Likely moat, if any:** the labeled weld-defect corpus and line-side calibration tooling, not the model architecture {INF}.
Runs on an edge PC at the station; results pushed to MES over OPC UA [3].

market.text: Initial wedge is weld QA in automotive body shops, with battery-pack and structural-casting inspection as adjacent expansions {INF}.
bullets: **Cognex / Keyence:** incumbent smart cameras with rules plus deep-learning add-ons; broad installed base and integrator channels.
**Internal OEM vision teams:** the real build-versus-buy alternative at large OEMs {INF}.
**Differentiation:** retraining speed and weld-specific defect taxonomy; durability depends on data scale {INF}.

sections.team_financing: CEO previously ran body-shop quality at a German OEM plant [4]; CTO holds a PhD in 3D vision [4]. Seed led by a regional industrial fund [2]. No follow-on round disclosed {UNK}.
sections.traction: Company reports two paid pilots and one production line at a Tier 1 supplier {CR}. No customer has confirmed publicly, and revenue is not disclosed {UNK}.

perspective.interesting: Retraining cost is the most common reason vision QA pilots fail to scale across lines; if onboarding time holds up in production, the unit of expansion is every new part variant {INF}.
perspective.validate: Whether the one production line is truly unassisted, and how much line-specific engineering each new deployment still needs.
perspective.fit: Fits the industrial AI and manufacturing focus; weld QA is relevant to automotive body shops broadly, so any Volkswagen Group angle should be tested rather than assumed {INF}.

questions.question: On the production line, how many engineer-days did onboarding the last new part variant take, and who did the labeling?
questions.why: Separates a product from a services business.

questions.question: What false-reject rate does the plant accept at line speed, and what is it today versus the pilot?
questions.why: Tests whether the system is trusted to run without manual re-inspection.

questions.question: What would it take for the Tier 1 to deploy on a second plant without Vireo engineers on site?
questions.why: Reveals deployment scalability and the real sales motion.
